lesson.title: Comparison Gym
lesson.subtitle: groter, kleiner, sneller, langzamer — compare without translating 'than'

hook.title: Put Two Things Side by Side
hook.content: Comparison only works when two things are on the table. Het huis is groter dan de kamer, de trein is sneller dan de fiets. The adjective changes; the frame does not.

pattern.title: Adjective + -er + dan
pattern.content: Groot → groter, klein → kleiner, snel → sneller, langzaam → langzamer. The second item follows dan. Use als only when the two are equal: even groot als.
pattern.trap_note: Langzaam is already an adjective; do not add meer. Langzamer, not meer langzaam.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Comparison Gym):
exercises.target_answer: groot, klein, snel, langzaam, goed, slecht
exercises.meaning: big, great, small, fast, slow, good, bad
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Comparison Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “The train is faster than the bike.”?
options: De trein is sneller dan de fiets.
De trein is sneller dan het fiets.
niet De trein is sneller dan de fiets.
exercises.target_answer: De trein is sneller dan de fiets.
exercises.meaning: The train is faster than the bike.
exercises.explanation: “De trein is sneller dan de fiets.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Comparison Gym”.

exercises.idea: The house is bigger than the room.
cues: It means: The house is bigger than the room.
idea_parts: The house is bigger than the room.
exercises.target_answer: Het huis is groter dan de kamer.
exercises.meaning: The house is bigger than the room.
exercises.explanation: “Het huis is groter dan de kamer.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Adjective + -er + dan.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Langzaam is already an adjective; do not add meer. Langzamer, not meer langzaam.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Zij werkt langzamer.” is word-for-word “She works slower.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Adjective + -er + dan.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: This book is better.
exercises.explanation: “Dit boek is beter.” reuses only material taught in “Comparison Gym” — Adjective + -er + dan.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Dit boek is beter.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Adjective + -er + dan.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “The car is faster than the bike.”
twist.target_answer: De auto is sneller dan de fiets.
twist.explanation: The same comparative frame with a different pair of nouns.

summary.outcome: Compare two nouns or actions with -er and dan.
summary.takeaway: Comparison is a frame for two items; the adjective carries the degree.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Pronouns & Possessives.

groot.etymology_derivation: English great and Dutch groot are the same word.

klein.etymology_derivation: English clean once meant 'small, fine'; Dutch kept klein for small.

snel.etymology_derivation: English snell is archaic; Dutch snel is everyday fast.

goed.etymology_derivation: English good and Dutch goed are the same word.

slecht.etymology_derivation: English slight is the old cousin; Dutch slecht means bad.
